title: Ubicloud PostgreSQL: New Features, Higher Performance
summary: Today, we are excited to announce a major upgrade to Ubicloud Postgres. The following features are now available as part of our managed service: Read Replicas, Scale Up/Down, Multi-AZ High Availability (HA), Connection Pooling, Managed Maintenance Window, Metrics, and External APIs.
body_text: Ubicloud PostgreSQL: New Features, Higher Performance May 20, 2025 · 5 min read Furkan Sahin Senior Software Engineer Postgres holds a special place for us. As the Ubicloud team, we built four managed Postgres solutions (including Heroku Postgres and Citus) over the years. When we launched Ubicloud Postgres last year , it was in a way our fifth managed Postgres service. From the outset, we mapped out the following feature list for our managed database. This list was based on hundreds of customer conversations; and we believed it to define a powerful managed PostgreSQL service. Today, we are excited to announce a major upgrade to Ubicloud Postgres. The following features are now available as part of our managed service: Read Replicas Scale up/down High Availability (HA) across multiple availability zones (multi-AZ) Connection pooling Managed Maintenance Window Metrics External APIs Read Replicas Read replicas allow you to create one or more copies of your primary PostgreSQL database instance. These replicas continuously follow your primary database using PostgreSQL’s replication mechanisms to stay up to date with changes. With Ubicloud, you can now spin up read replicas with a single click. Why Read Replicas Matter? Scalability and isolation: Read replicas empower you to scale your database horizontally, distributing read-heavy workloads-such as reporting, analytics, and real-time dashboards-across multiple dedicated replicas. By directing analytical and business intelligence queries to these replicas, you keep your primary instance focused and responsive for write operations and critical transactional workloads. This separation also ensures that your core application remains isolated from unpredictable or resource-intensive queries run by analysts or reporting tools. Business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR): Read replicas can play a critical role in case of a primary database failure, a read replica can be promoted to primary, ensuring minimal downtime and data loss. Scale Up/Down With Ubicloud, you can resize your database instance according to the needs of your business with just a few clicks. Scaling up or down is one of the simplest ways to keep your managed PostgreSQL database both high-performing and cost-effective, no matter how your needs evolve. Why Scale Up/Down? Prepare for Growth: Instantly scale up ahead of product launches, seasonal spikes, or intensive analytics workloads to ensure top performance. Optimize for Cost: Scale down during quieter periods to reduce costs, so you only pay for what you need. Stay Agile: Respond to changing trends without overprovisioning or manual intervention High Availability Across Multiple Datacenters (Multi-AZ) High Availability (HA) is critical for any production database. Ubicloud Managed PostgreSQL now supports HA configurations across multiple datacenters (multi-AZ). This means that your managed database spans across availability zones, ensuring your application stays online even if an entire datacenter experiences an outage. Ubicloud PostgreSQL’s automated failover ensures minimal downtime and seamless continuity for your applications. How It Works In the Ubicloud dashboard, enable high availability and select your preferred standby count. Ubicloud provisions your primary instance and up to two standby servers across separate data-centers. Replication is managed automatically - your data stays in sync and we automatically failover to a standby in case of a failure. In the event of a data center failure, we automatically redirect traffic to a healthy standby in another data center. Next up Quick Start - Build your own cloud Connection Pooling (PgBouncer) Connection pooling is now built into Ubicloud PostgreSQL, making it more performant and scalable. Why Connection Pooling? PostgreSQL performance can degrade with the number of parallel connections because PostgreSQL creates a new backend process for every client connection. This can quickly consume memory and CPU as your application grows. Connection pooling improves database performance by managing persistent connections, instead of constantly opening and closing them. This reduces latency and increases throughput. It’s especially beneficial for applications that make numerous short, intermittent database requests. Ubicloud uses PgBouncer, the industry-standard connection pooler for PostgreSQL. You can start using it simply by updating your application’s connection string to point to the port 6432, instead of the default port 5432. Firewall rules are applied the same way to the pooling port as well. With built-in connection pooling, Ubicloud PostgreSQL provides a high performance, stable and reliable PostgreSQL experience. Managed Maintenance Windows A managed maintenance window lets you control when essential updates-like configuration changes, minor updates, and system improvements-are applied to your managed PostgreSQL instance. Instead of unexpected interruptions, you decide the best time for maintenance, ensuring your database stays secure and up-to-date with minimal impact on your application. How It Works In the Ubicloud dashboard, you can set a preferred maintenance window for each managed PostgreSQL instance. Ubicloud will automatically apply updates only during your chosen window, keeping you in control of when changes happen. Maintenance operations are fully managed: you don’t need to monitor or manually apply patches-Ubicloud handles it for you. Metrics Our UI now has all the metrics you need to keep track of your database usage. You can see metrics like CPU, memory or disk usage at 15 seconds granularity. This way, you can diagnose and resolve issues that might degrade your database performance. You can also decide to scale your database according to your needs. Manage Everything Through APIs Ubicloud PostgreSQL is designed for automation and integration from the ground up. Every major operation can be performed programmatically through our APIs. These operations include creating databases, scaling resources, enabling or disabling high availability (HA), provisioning read replicas, and more. With Ubicloud’s API-first approach, you’re in control - whether you’re managing a single instance or orchestrating multiple databases across regions. Conclusion Ubicloud PostgreSQL brings together years of expertise and a focus on what matters most: reliability, performance, and control. With our new features, you have the tools you need to build on a modern PostgreSQL database. What sets Ubicloud apart from other solutions are: We use local NVMes. This helps us deliver price/performance that’s 7.9 - 11.1x better than Aurora PostgreSQL. We have years of experience with PostgreSQL. This makes us keep reliability as a forethought when releasing new features. We provide the first open-source solution for managed PostgreSQL. This keeps you in control of your database. If you have questions or feedback, our team would love to hear from you at [email protected] .

title: HCG Test Negative But Pregnant? Here’s Why
summary: An hCG test that’s negative but you’re pregnant can be confusing. Learn the common causes of false negative pregnancy tests and the steps to take next.
body_text: Getting a negative result from a home pregnancy test (HPT) when you know you’re pregnant can be confusing and distressing. How can your hCG test be negative when you’re actually pregnant? Though HPTs are 99% accurate when used correctly, false negative pregnancy test results can happen. There are many reasons why this is possible, even with a blood hCG test. Let’s look at the most frequent causes of a negative hCG test even if you’re pregnant. Plus, what you should do about it. Key Takeaways A negative test doesn’t always mean you’re not pregnant. Testing too early is the most common cause of a false result. Home tests need about 20-25 mIU/mL of hCG to register a positive result. This is a threshold many pregnancies haven’t reached until the day of a missed period. Diluted urine, low-sensitivity test kits, user error, ectopic pregnancy, and the hook effect (from very high hCG, often with twins) can all cause a false negative. If symptoms like a missed period or nausea persist, retest in 48–72 hours with first-morning urine. Or, ask your provider for a blood test, which is the most reliable way to confirm pregnancy. Pregnancy symptoms can overlap with PMS, so they’re not a reliable sign on their own. But if you think you’re pregnant, have symptoms, and keep getting a negative test, it’s worth a call to your healthcare provider. This is not the time to wait and see. How do home pregnancy tests work? Every pregnancy test, home or clinical, is looking for one thing: a hormone called human chorionic gonadotropin hCG. The embryo starts producing hCG before implantation . After attachment of the embryo to the uterine lining (implantation), the developing placenta takes over hCG production and levels begin to rise rapidly. Levels roughly double every two days for the first 8-10 weeks. hCG itself is made of two parts: alpha and beta. The structure of the alpha subunit is identical to that of a few other hormones (FSH, LH, TSH). But the beta subunit is unique to hCG. This is why you’ll see beta hCG on more precise tests. There are also two ways to test for it: Qualitative hCG blood tests : Just confirm whether hCG is there (this is how most home urine tests work) Quantitative tests: Measure the exact amount Home urine pregnancy tests (UPTs) work by testing your urine for hCG. You can either hold the test stick in your urine stream or dip the tip into a clean cup of collected urine. Inside that strip, there are antibodies waiting to grab onto hCG if it’s there. This forms what’s called a “ sandwich complex ” that triggers a color change. Two lines = positive One line = negative Used correctly, home pregnancy tests have been shown to have sensitivity up to 100% and specificity around 99.2% . That word “correctly” matters, though. Most home tests need your hCG to hit somewhere around 20-25 mIU/mL before they’ll flag it. This usually lines up with about four weeks post-conception . One study found that at 11 days past ovulation, the typical hCG level was about 25.04 mIU/mL. This is right on the edge of what a home urine test can catch, meaning about half of pregnant women testing that early can get a negative test result. A day or two before that, at 9-10 DPO, average levels were closer to 0.93 mIU/mL — nowhere near enough to register. This is exactly why the standard advice is to wait until the first day of a missed period before you test. Know more: How Long After Implantation Does hCG Rise? Blood tests work the same basic way, but they check your blood sample instead of your urine. Because hCG shows up in blood before it’s filtered into urine , blood tests tend to catch pregnancy earlier. They can also measure your exact hCG number rather than just yes or no. So why would a real pregnancy test negative? A few factors can throw off a home pregnancy test, even when you’re pregnant. Here’s what might be going on. You tested too early. This is by far the most common reason. Implantation doesn’t happen on the same day for everyone. One study found: 29% of pregnancies had implanted six days before a missed period 40% by five days before 76% by four days before This means a large number of women testing early simply haven’t built up enough hCG yet, regardless of how sensitive the test is. That’s why testing is recommended on or after the first day of your missed period . This allows time for nearly all pregnancies to implant and for hCG levels to be detectable. Of course, that’s only useful if you know when your period is due. Even with regular cycles, ovulation doesn’t always occur on the same day every month, and for those with irregular cycles that “wait and see” advice can feel like more guesswork. This is where tracking your hormones directly, rather than counting days on a calendar, makes the timing clearer. The Inito Fertility Monitor tracks your FSH, LH, estrogen, and PdG levels to predict and confirm ovulation. This means you know your actual ovulation day, as well as how many days post ovulation (DPO) you are and, thus, can know the right day to test. Your urine was too diluted. If you’re drinking a lot of water before testing, your urine (and your hCG) gets diluted with it. And early on in your pregnancy, when hCG levels may not be as high to begin with, this can make all the difference between a positive and a negative test. However, some pick up on lower hCG levels than others, so the same urine sample could read negative on one brand and positive on another. But to err on the side of precaution, use your first-morning urine to take a test. Something went wrong with the test itself. Expired, stored wrong, or read at the wrong time — any of these things can throw off a result even when enough hCG is present. It may be an ectopic pregnancy. When a pregnancy implants outside the uterus, hCG tends to rise more slowly or abnormally . This can mean a negative test despite a real pregnancy. Ectopic pregnancy is a medical emergency. So if you have belly pain, bleeding, dizziness, or fainting, get medical help right away. This is true whether you tested positive or not. You’re pregnant with twins. This is the surprising one. You’d think more hCG would be a test more likely to catch it. But at extremely high levels (like you get with twins or multiple pregnancies), hCG can actually overwhelm the antibodies on the test strip. This is called the hook effect or prozone phenomenon . The tests can’t process the hormone correctly, so you get a negative not because there’s too little hCG, but because there’s too much. Know more: Can Twins Cause a False Negative Pregnancy Test? Even blood tests aren’t immune. They’re more sensitive than urine tests, but they can still miss an early pregnancy if drawn too soon after conception. What should you do if you think you’re pregnant and get a false negative test? If you’re having any of these symptoms of pregnancy : A missed period Sore breasts Nausea Fatigue Needing to pee constantly Mild cramping Implantation bleeding , But the tests say no? Don’t take that as the final answer. Here’s what to do instead: Wait 48-72 hours and test again. Test first thing in the morning when your urine is most concentrated. Make sure the test isn’t expired and follow the instructions exactly. If your period still hasn’t shown up or your symptoms are sticking around, see your healthcare provider for a blood test. It’s a simple draw that will confirm pregnancy. You may need an ultrasound too if your doctor advises. Why is retesting important? Though rare, a false negative doesn’t just cost you a little confusion. It can delay a diagnosis that matters. This includes diagnosing an ectopic pregnancy early, when treatment is most effective. Research shows false negatives happen more in women who already have symptoms like abdominal pain and bleeding. This is exactly when you don’t want to be relying on one urine test alone. If your gut is telling you something the stick isn’t, trust it enough to check again. A serum beta-hCG blood test is considered the gold standard for confirming or ruling out pregnancy. Think of it like a tie breaker. Conclusion A negative hCG pregnancy test feels definitive, but it isn’t always. Most of the time, a false negative just means you tested a little too early. Less often, it’s: Diluted urine A less sensitive kit User error An ectopic pregnancy Hook effect from very high hCG If your body is telling you one thing and the test is telling you another, give it a few days and try again. Make sure to use first-morning urine and follow the instructions exactly. And if things aren’t adding up? Let your doctor run a blood test. You deserve a real answer, not just a guess. FAQs What are some reasons you can get a negative pregnancy test while pregnant? Testing too early is the big one. It can also be caused by: Diluted urine A less sensitive test User error Ectopic pregnancy The hook effect from very high hCG (rarely seen though) What should I do if I get a negative pregnancy test but still think I'm pregnant? Wait 48–72 hours and test again with first-morning urine. If: Your period still doesn’t come Symptoms continue You develop severe pain or heavy bleeding, contact your healthcare provider. They might recommend a blood hCG test and further evaluation. Can you be pregnant with a negative hCG test? Yes. Testing too early is the most likely explanation. Less commonly, an ectopic pregnancy or the hook effect can cause a negative result even when you’re pregnant. Can I be 5 weeks pregnant and still get a negative test? It’s uncommon, but a less sensitive test, diluted urine, or an ectopic pregnancy could explain it. A blood hCG test can give you a clear answer. Is it possible to be pregnant but have no hCG at all? No. A viable pregnancy would have hCG. The embryo starts making small amounts of hCG before implantation, and levels rise after implantation. This is because the developing placenta becomes the main source of production. Early on, hCG might just be too low for a home pregnancy test to detect it. Can I be 2 months pregnant and still test negative? It would be unusual. By then, hCG is typically well above what any test needs. If it happens, see your doctor. They might order a blood hCG test and an ultrasound to determine the cause. Is it possible to be 7 weeks pregnant and still test negative? It’s rare, but the hook effect from very high hCG (like with twins) might cause false negative results. A blood test can sort it out. Can twins cause a false negative pregnancy test at 7 weeks? Yes, in rare cases. Twin pregnancies can push hCG high enough to overwhelm the test strip, causing a negative despite a real pregnancy. How long until a negative pregnancy test after a miscarriage at 5 weeks? It depends on how high your hCG was to start. It can take anywhere from a few days to a few weeks to clear your system. Your doctor can track this with repeat blood tests. How much hCG is needed to confirm pregnancy? Most home tests need 20–25 mIU/mL. Blood tests can detect much lower amounts, which is why doctors use them to confirm pregnancy earlier or clear up an unclear result. What are the signs of a hidden or unconfirmed pregnancy? Missed period, sore breasts, nausea, fatigue, frequent urination, mild cramping, and light implantation bleeding. All of these are possible even if a test reads negative. How quickly is hCG positive? Most tests turn positive around the time your period would be due. This is about 12–14 days past ovulation, once hCG has had time to build up. Can twins give a negative pregnancy test? Yes, through the hook effect. Extremely high hCG from a multiple pregnancy can actually overwhelm the test and give you a false negative result. Why am I pregnant but keep testing negative? Most likely, you tested too early. Less commonly, diluted urine, a less sensitive test, user error, ectopic pregnancy, or the hook effect could be behind it.

title: Braiin Limited Announces Commencement of Trading on Split-Adjusted Basis Following Three-for-One Stock Split

title: AOP and Ipsos: 37% of people don't know AI can fabricate, and its most trusting users stop at the answer
summary: Ipsos research for the Association of Online Publishers finds people increasingly take AI answers on trust: 37% don't know AI tools can fabricate, and a third of the most trusting users never click past the answer.
body_text: People are handing more of their questions to AI assistants, and new research puts numbers on how much of what comes back gets taken on faith. The Artificial Intelligence Publisher Impact Study, conducted by Ipsos for the UK's Association of Online Publishers on a nationally representative sample of 1,000 people, finds that 37% of respondents do not know AI tools can fabricate information, Press Gazette reports . Among 45-to-54-year-olds the share rises to 45%. The behavior data points the same way. When respondents completely trust the material an answer draws on, their confidence in the AI answer runs above 90%, and 32% of those most trusting users show what the study calls "stop here" behavior: they take the answer as delivered and click nothing further. The research was sponsored by a publisher trade body with its own stake in the findings, which is worth noting, but the sample is nationally representative and the pattern holds across the study. The direction of travel is the story. AI assistants are moving from novelty to advisor: people ask, get an answer, and act on it. A user who does not know the tool can fabricate has no reason to verify anything, and a user who trusts what they are shown clicks nothing. Both groups experience the AI's answer as the information itself, not as a pointer to it. The takeaway for brands: for a growing share of your buyers, what an AI model says about you is the final word, not the starting point for research. Nobody in that 32% is clicking through to your site to double-check. The model's opinion of your brand, formed from everything it has read, is the version of you those buyers meet, which makes knowing what AI believes about your brand , and correcting it where it is wrong, a first-order marketing problem rather than a curiosity.

title: Cultural Competence & Language Access for Providers
summary: How providers build strong cultural competence in healthcare: training, nursing, counseling, and Section 1557 compliance. July 2026.
body_text: One in five American households speaks a language other than English at home, and that number has held steady in reports for years while language access keeps getting filed under "nice to have." If your care team still leans on family members to relay diagnoses, cultural competence in healthcare is not happening, no matter how many training hours your staff has logged. TLDR: Language barriers cause detectable physical harm in over 49% of affected patients, driving readmissions and adverse events (Divi et al., 2007). Section 1557's 2024 final rule requires free, qualified language assistance; organizations with 15+ employees must name a coordinator. Cultural competence and cultural humility work together: knowledge without self-reflection hardens into stereotype. Strong training covers implicit bias, interpreter protocols, and cross-cultural communication, and never stops at a one-time session. What cultural competence in healthcare means Cultural competence in healthcare is the ability of providers and their organizations to deliver care that meets the social, cultural, and linguistic needs of every patient. It works on two levels: the clinician who adapts how they communicate, assess, and treat, and the system around them, including policies, staffing, and language services. Two anchors shape most definitions. The Cross et al. framework, developed in 1989, described a set of behaviors and attitudes that let systems work well in cross-cultural situations. The National CLAS Standards, from the Office of Minority Health, translate that into practical expectations. Both treat language access in healthcare as a baseline, not an add-on. Why language is the foundation of cultural competence A provider can respect a patient's beliefs and still send them home with the wrong instructions. Attitude is invisible when the words do not land. Every clinical encounter runs through language, the channel where cultural competence either shows up or quietly breaks. Consider what depends on shared understanding: History-taking, where a missed detail changes the working diagnosis Informed consent, which is only informed if the patient grasps the risks Diagnosis, built on symptoms the patient can describe and the provider can hear Patient education, from wound care to warning signs Medication adherence, where dosing confusion becomes a readmission Cultural awareness sets the intent. Language access carries it into the room. The clinical cost of language barriers A patient nods along to discharge instructions she cannot fully follow. That gap has a body count. A large share of patients with limited English proficiency arrive already at a disadvantage. Language barriers have been linked to detectable physical harm in just over 49% of affected patients, according to research on language barriers in care . The pattern shows up in metrics leaders already track: Higher 30-day readmission rates Longer emergency department stays Increased rates of adverse events Analysis of patient safety ties these outcomes to breakdowns in shared understanding. Cultural competence vs. cultural humility Two terms travel together in training decks, and providers often treat them as synonyms. They are not. Cultural competence implies a body of knowledge you acquire, a checklist of customs you learn about a group. Cultural humility takes a different stance: an ongoing, self-reflective practice that admits your own bias and treats the patient as the authority on their experience. Humility without grounding leaves you improvising. Research from Boston Medical Center frames them as complementary. Language access serves both: it gives competence facts a patient can correct, and it makes humility possible, because cultural intelligence in medical interpretation means you cannot center a voice you cannot hear. Examples of cultural competence in healthcare Abstract principles help nobody at the bedside. Here is what cultural competence looks like in a real encounter. Bringing in a qualified interpreter for a diagnostic conversation instead of leaning on the patient's teenage daughter to relay a cancer diagnosis. Handing over discharge instructions in the patient's language, using plain language principles , so the care plan survives the trip home. Reading a patient's silence as deference to authority, and checking understanding before you assume consent. Adapting dietary guidance to cultural and religious practices, so a diabetes plan fits the food a family actually eats. Asking about traditional healing practices, then folding them in where safe. Each depends on communication that lands. Cultural competence in nursing Nurses see patients more than anyone on the care team, which puts them first in line to catch a language or cultural barrier before it becomes preventable harm in healthcare . Cultural competence shows up across their day: Intake, where a careful history depends on the patient feeling heard Medication education, where dosing confusion turns into a missed dose at home Discharge teaching, where understanding decides whether the plan holds Care coordination, where handoffs carry cultural context alongside orders Nursing programs now build these frameworks into the curriculum. Culturally aware care measurably improves patient trust, adherence, and safety. Cultural competence in counseling and behavioral health Behavioral health runs almost entirely on words. There is no lab value for grief, no imaging for a panic attack. When language and culture misalign, the whole encounter wobbles. Two problems stack up. Patients facing language barriers avoid mental health care, so those who show up are often already in crisis. And when they speak, distress rarely translates cleanly. A patient describing "nerves" or a physical ache may be naming depression, easily missed as a somatic complaint. Culturally specific expressions of grief can read as psychosis to an unfamiliar clinician. Stigma around mental illness shapes what a patient will admit, and to whom. Misread any of these, and misdiagnosis follows. Understanding medical translator vs. interpreter differences matters especially in behavioral health. Section 1557 and the legal case for language access Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act carries teeth. The 2024 final rule , currently in effect as of mid-2026, requires covered entities to provide free, timely, and qualified language assistance and to: Post notices of availability in your state's top 15 languages Designate a Section 1557 coordinator if you are a covered entity with 15 or more employees Train staff on written language-access policies Fall short, and you risk federal penalties and lost funding. What cultural competence training in healthcare should include Strong training moves past a single slideshow. It builds repeatable skills your staff can use in the next visit, and it works at two levels: the individual clinician and the organization that sets policy. A solid program covers: Implicit bias awareness, so providers catch assumptions before they reach the patient Cross-cultural communication techniques for checking understanding Language-access policies and clear escalation protocols How to work with a qualified interpreter without sidelining the patient Recognizing cultural health beliefs and traditional practices Documentation practices for interpreted encounters One-time sessions fade. Treat competency as ongoing development, refreshed and audited. Building a language-access program that supports cultural competence A functioning language-access program is the infrastructure cultural competence runs on. Treat it as a system with moving parts, each assigned an owner. Assess community language needs, so your service map matches the patients who actually walk in. Put written policies on paper, covering when and how interpretation is offered. Select qualified interpretation services, weighing AI interpretation vs. phone interpreter services , for spoken and written needs across the languages your data flags. Train clinical and front-desk staff, since access fails at the first hello if registration cannot route a patient. Define escalation procedures for high-risk encounters, naming which visits demand a human interpreter. Monitor quality through audits and error review. Track utilization by language and department, then act on the gaps. Skip the tracking, and you are guessing. A program you cannot measure is a checkbox, and a checkbox does not keep patients safe. How Opalite Health supports language-access and cultural competence at the point of care Everything above describes the work. Here is where we fit into it. Opalite Health is a physician-led AI interpreter for healthcare built for real-time clinical conversation across more than 150 languages and dialects. We give your care team three things at the point of care: Instant interpretation, so a provider never waits for a line to connect Multilingual AI scribing that captures a cross-language encounter as structured clinical documentation Medical document translation for discharge instructions, consent forms, and patient education materials We are HIPAA compliant and integrate with leading EHRs, including Epic and Cerner. Our interpretation accuracy is documented in a Johns Hopkins Medicine study and is auditable at the encounter level. One caution worth stating plainly: Opalite works alongside qualified human interpreters within a risk-based language-access program, not to replace them. High-risk encounters still call for a human. We help you cover the rest. What strong cultural competence in healthcare actually requires Cultural humility, training, and policy all matter. So does the moment a patient sits down and your team cannot fully hear them. A missed discharge instruction, a consent form the patient cannot read, a diagnosis relayed through a family member who is guessing at the words: these are the gaps that drive readmissions, adverse events, and liability. Good care travels through language, and your program is only as strong as that connection. See Opalite Health in action to learn how AI interpretation supports your team across 150+ languages.
